title: Email extraction not working from websites
description: During testing with 'gyms in New York', zero emails were extracted from any of the 3 business websites, despite all sites being successfully accessed (HTTP 200). The regex pattern at scraper/scrape.py:75-76 may need review, or sites may have obfuscated emails. Consider using BeautifulSoup for better HTML parsing.

title: bug
description: When user clicks stop scraping button during scraping, the partial results are saved to Excel but not displayed on the UI. Expected behavior: Partial results should be displayed, processed, and shown in the UI exactly like full results. User should see the scraped data table and be able to download it. Currently the data disappears after stop is clicked.
close_reason: Implemented incremental data saving during scraping. Partial results are now preserved when stop button is clicked and displayed on UI automatically. Added data callback to save each scraped business to session state immediately.

title: Review Count extraction failing - all showing NaN
description: During testing with 'gyms in New York', all 3 scraped businesses showed NaN for Review Count. The XPath selector at scraper/scrape.py:119-127 needs to be updated to match current Google Maps HTML structure. Add fallback selectors and better error handling.
notes: Fixed with improved selectors and smart wait logic. Review count now extracting successfully using multiple fallback selectors and aria-label parsing. Test shows 100% extraction rate.

title: Duplicate log entries in Streamlit app
description:
The Streamlit-based UI currently writes multiple identical log lines for single user actions (e.g., workflow mode selection, file uploads, and Start Scraping clicks). This makes  noisy and harder to inspect when users send logs for support, as seen in recent runs where each event appears 4–6 times.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each logical user action (mode change, Start Scraping click, file upload, existing file load, save) should result in at most one log line per run, or a clearly grouped set for a single scrape run.
- Ensure Streamlit reruns do not cause duplicated log records for the same interaction.
- Keep the logging verbose enough for support (queries, paths, row counts, errors) but deduplicated and easy to read.
- Confirm behavior both in dev (Python script) and in the packaged Windows .exe.

title: Implement smart wait logic with configurable retries for scraping reliability
description: Replace hardcoded time.sleep() with intelligent WebDriverWait + ExpectedConditions. Issues: (1) Fixed waits fail on slow connections, (2) No retry logic for elements, (3) No verification that elements loaded before proceeding. Solution: Add configurable wait/retry settings to config, implement exponential backoff, use explicit waits for all elements (search box, results feed, business cards, info panels). Make wait times and retry attempts configurable.
notes: Implemented smart wait logic: Created wait_utils.py with SmartWait class, added WAIT_CONFIG to settings, updated search.py and scrape.py to use explicit waits instead of fixed sleeps. Now waits for elements to appear with configurable timeouts and retry logic.
